security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives. The skill still includes command-based workflow steps and a prompt-injection risk because it tells agents to obey system_instructions from JSON task files. Remove delegated system authority and add explicit safeguards around script execution and logging.

remediation.issue: Untrusted task JSON can define system_instructions that the agent is told to follow as hard constraints.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this delegation and state that task file content is untrusted data. Define allowed task fields without granting instruction authority.

remediation.issue: The workflow instructs agents to run local repository scripts for fetch, submit, and flag operations.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each command and document expected script paths, dry-run behavior, and side effects.

remediation.issue: Raw JSONL execution event logging may capture sensitive task content.
remediation.suggestion: Document log retention, redaction, access controls, and when logging should be disabled for sensitive material.

content.value_statement: Historical evidence reviews can miss forced surrender cues, procedural irregularities, and consent issues. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured JSON-only review workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides review of Coercion_Duress JSON task batches for forced surrenders, threats, and consent issues.
Defines output fields for provenance, reliability, OCR status, evidence quotes, and page references.
Requires verbatim evidence extraction and neutral factual summaries without legal conclusions.
Provides validation checks for metadata, minimum narrative length, date format, and banned opinion words.
Describes a command-based workflow for fetching, submitting, and flagging tasks through refinement_workflow.py.
Explains flag reasons for irrelevant, OCR failure, and provenance failure cases.
limitations: It is not a legal opinion tool and forbids conclusions such as proving fraud.
It requires existing repository scripts and JSON task files, so it is not self-contained.
It does not verify external sources beyond task content and referenced provenance fields.
Its command examples can modify local workflow state when they are run.

use_cases.title: Index forced surrender evidence
use_cases.description: Review task batches for threats, pressure language, and consent problems while preserving exact quotes.

use_cases.title: Prepare neutral evidence summaries
use_cases.description: Convert document excerpts into factual summaries with provenance, reliability, OCR status, and page references.

use_cases.title: Validate Coercion_Duress submissions
use_cases.description: Check metadata, banned words, date format, and manager review status before workflow submission.

prompt_templates.title: Review one task batch
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a Coercion_Duress input file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the coercion-duress skill to review one Coercion_Duress task batch. Extract only factual evidence about threats, pressure, consent, and procedure.

prompt_templates.title: Build citation-ready summaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate evidence extraction with page anchors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this batch and prepare neutral summaries with document identifiers, dates, provenance, reliability, OCR status, verbatim quotes, and page references.

prompt_templates.title: Flag workflow exceptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage for poor input quality or provenance gaps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the task set for corrupt text, irrelevant material, OCR failure, or provenance failure. State the proper flag reason for each exception.

prompt_templates.title: Audit before submission
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pre-flight review of completed analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the completed Coercion_Duress analysis against the skill rules. Find missing metadata, opinion words, weak citations, short summaries, and premature conclusions.

output_examples.input: A task batch contains correspondence about a surrender meeting and disputed signatures.
output_examples.output: The review identifies the document title, date, provenance, reliability, OCR status, exact pressure language, and page anchors for each relevant passage.

output_examples.input: A task has garbled OCR text and no usable document context.
output_examples.output: The result records an OCR failure recommendation and avoids adding unsupported evidence summaries.

output_examples.input: A completed analysis uses words such as likely and suggests.
output_examples.output: The pre-flight review marks those terms for removal and replaces them with factual wording tied to direct quotes.

best_practices: Read the full super task before judging relevance or extracting evidence.
Use verbatim quotes and page anchors when the task includes usable evidence.
Run pre-flight checks for metadata, date format, length, and opinion words before submission.
anti_patterns: Using keyword matches instead of reading the surrounding context.
Returning Unknown for metadata that appears in the task text.
Treating workflow submissions as final before manager approval.

faq.question: What documents does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Coercion_Duress JSON task batches that contain historical document excerpts and metadata.

faq.question: Does it provide legal conclusions?
faq.answer: No. It requires neutral summaries, verbatim evidence, and factual context only.

faq.question: Can it analyze PDFs directly?
faq.answer: No. The instructions limit the workflow to JSON input and JSON output.

faq.question: What evidence does it prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes threats, forced surrender language, consent problems, translation issues, and procedural irregularities.

faq.question: Why are metadata checks required?
faq.answer: Metadata checks keep document identifiers, dates, provenance, reliability, and OCR status consistent for later review.

faq.question: Does it need local scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. The described fetch, submit, and flag workflow depends on repository scripts.
